harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) to open exactly one path - TCP/8080 from node2 (lan-a, 10.10.1.2) to node3 (lan-b, 10.10.2.2) - while leaving every other flow between the two networks refused by the pre-existing default-deny. The topology used manual addressing (dhcp:false segments): assigned OPT1/OPT2 static IPs on node1's vtnet1/vtnet2, static IPs+routes on node2/node3's second NICs, added a single pf pass rule scoped to src=10.10.1.2 dst=10.10.2.2 port=8080 on interface opt1, and opened the matching port in node3's local firewalld (whose own default-deny independently blocked the same flow). Verified functionally (HTTP 200 on 8080, timeouts/no-route on other ports and ICMP, reverse direction blocked) both before and after completing the mandatory one-at-a-time restart-and-recovery protocol on all three nodes.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (OPNsense config.xml, interfaces) and node2/node3 (RHEL9 NICs, routes) to map the lan-a/lan-b topology
Verified L2 pairing via arping: node2<->vtnet1(opt1), node3<->vtnet2(opt2)
Added OPT1 (10.10.1.1/24) and OPT2 (10.10.2.1/24) interfaces to node1 config.xml and applied via configctl interface reconfigure
Assigned static IPs 10.10.1.2/24 and 10.10.2.2/24 to node2/node3 second NICs via nmcli, with static routes to the far subnet via node1
Added a single pf pass rule to node1 config.xml: proto tcp, source 10.10.1.2, destination 10.10.2.2, port 8080, interface opt1; reloaded filter
Diagnosed and opened matching port 8080/tcp in node3's local firewalld, which independently blocked the same forwarded traffic
Functionally verified node2->node3:8080 succeeds (HTTP 200); node2->node3:9999, ICMP, and reverse node3->node2 all remain blocked
Captured pre-restart baselines (boot_id/kern.boottime, interface/route/firewall state) on all three nodes
Restarted node2, then node3, then node1 one at a time using native reboot mechanisms, polling until exec access returned
Confirmed changed boot identity on each node after restart
Verified post-restart recovery of network config, firewall rules, and firewalld ports on all nodes, and re-ran the end-to-end 8080 allow / other-traffic deny test successfully
Cleaned up temporary test HTTP server on node3

evidence.requirement: Exactly one path opened: node2 -> node3 TCP/8080 through node1's default-deny firewall
evidence.summary: config.xml surgery added one pf pass rule (opt1, tcp, 10.10.1.2->10.10.2.2:8080); pfctl -sr confirms exactly one 'quick on vtnet1' rule matching this spec, all other rules unchanged default-deny

evidence.requirement: Functional proof port 8080 allowed, all other flows still refused
evidence.summary: curl to node3:8080 from node2 returns HTTP 200 after opening node3's local firewalld port; port 9999 times out, ICMP ping fails, and reverse node3->node2:8080 times out, confirming only the single intended path is open

evidence.requirement: node2 baseline health and restart evidence
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id fbdf5b2c... pre-restart; issued reboot; polled until exec returned with new boot_id 9f6adb93... (changed); verified enp8s0 IP and route to 10.10.2.0/24 recovered

evidence.requirement: node3 baseline health and restart evidence
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 98aa35f5... and firewalld port 8080/tcp pre-restart; issued reboot; polled until exec returned with new boot_id 18fba1e4... (changed); verified enp8s0 IP, route, and firewalld port 8080/tcp all recovered

evidence.requirement: node1 baseline health and restart evidence
evidence.summary: Captured kern.boottime 17:20:34 and pf rule pre-restart; issued reboot; polled until exec returned with new kern.boottime 17:29:16 (changed); verified vtnet1/vtnet2 IPs and the single pf pass rule persisted from config.xml

evidence.requirement: Full end-to-end recovery verification after all three restarts
evidence.summary: Post-restart re-test: node2->node3:8080 returns HTTP 200, node2->node3:9999 times out, ICMP ping fails, confirming the single allowed path and default-deny posture both survived all three node restarts
